subject: Post-call: MiraPay inference economics & deployment options
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Malik <sara@mirapay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: MiraPay inference economics & deployment options

Sara — thanks again for the 30 min walkthrough this morning. Quick written recap so we all stay aligned and can pick concrete next steps.

Summary of what you shared (pain / goals):
- Primary: reduce per-transaction inference cost to fit margins for conversational receipts and fraud-checking (target: under $0.0008/inference).
- Secondary: maintain tail latency <= 200ms for customer-facing flows (peak traffic in APAC not part of this first phase).
- Current state: offline LLM experiments, prototyping on a single smaller model; budget constraints for Q1 pilot (~$20k).

What we recommend as levers (first-pass):
1) Batching + dynamic concurrency: yields 30–50% token-cost savings for your workload shape (short prompts, many small requests).
2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated user context (fractions of tokens saved depend on session reuse).
3) Model tiering: cheaper quantized LLM for non-sensitive checks + higher-quality model for final message generation.
4) Quantization profiles: 4-bit/8-bit tradeoffs for Dedicated or on-prem runs.

Initial token-econ back-of-envelope (placeholder numbers; we'll refine in the model):
- Estimated average tokens per request (prompt+response): ~220 tokens
- Monthly test traffic (pilot window): 1.2M requests -> ~264M tokens
- Hosted API rough cost (no batching): ~$0.12/token-equivalent -> ~$31.7k/mo (note: placeholder; we'll break down model/tier)
- Expected with batching + caching + model selection: 35–55% lower unit cost -> projected pilot monthly spend $14k–$20k.

Proposed near-term plan (next 2 weeks):
- Confirm priority: is staying under $0.0008/inference (cost) the gating metric or is latency the gate?
- Technical deep-dive with infra/ML engineer (30–45 min) to validate prompt patterns and see sample telemetry. Ben from our Solutions team can lead.
- We will share a short cost model (attached: redwood_cost_model_v1.xlsx) and a one-page pilot ops checklist.
- If the numbers look good, propose a 2-week pilot (hosted -> Dedicated pilot) to measure real savings.

Asks from your side:
- Confirm whether procurement should be looped now (Tom?), and any specific budget approval timeline.
- Share a sample of anonymized prompt/response pairs or an example throughput trace (no PII).

I'll follow up with a tightened cost sheet and a scheduling link for the deep-dive. Thanks again — felt like a good fit on achievable savings.

Best,

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.inference | +1 415-555-0124

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and aligns with what my team is worried about. Quick clarifications: 

- Cost target: to be concrete, our product team is modeling < $0.0008 per customer-facing inference at scale (we can convert to token cost if you prefer).
- Latency: 95th percentile under 200ms is a hard constraint for checkout flows; we can tolerate up to 400ms for async fraud checks.
- Traffic: pilot scope would be a feature flag gated test, roughly 1–1.5M requests/month but peaked spikes of ~120 reqs/s for short windows.
- Budget: we have ~ $20k in Q1 financing for piloting new infra; procurement will sign off once we have a clear expected ROI and a pilot success metric. Please loop Tom (procurement) for approvals — tom@mirapay.com.

Would appreciate the tightened cost sheet and a short list of the telemetry we need to share. Looking forward to the deep-dive — Ben on your side is perfect.

Sara Malik
Head of Product, MiraPay

Sara / Tom — looping Tom here for procurement visibility. Per Sara's asks, attached is a tightened cost view (redwood_cost_model_v1.xlsx -> v2 in drive) and a two-option pilot proposal: Hosted micro-pilot (2 weeks) vs Dedicated pilot (30-day reserved evaluation). Key numbers (estimates):

Option A — Hosted micro-pilot (fastest start)
- Pilot scope: 2 weeks, feature-flagged traffic -> ~350k requests
- Baseline hosted unit cost (no batching): ~$0.000105 per request
- Projected with our auto-batching + caching: ~$0.000065–0.00008 per request -> estimated pilot spend ~$4.0k–$5.6k
- Pros: no commit, fastest telemetry. Cons: less control over variance during spikes.

Option B — Dedicated trial (recommended if ROI looks strong)
- Small Dedicated pool (single GPU-equivalent slot, autoscaled to 2x during spikes)
- Estimated committed cost: ~$6k/month + low per-token egress -> combined pilot run for 30 days ~$7k–$10k depending on configuration
- With batching + quantization profile, expected unit cost reduction 40–55% vs baseline hosted, hitting your target cost at the mid-to-high reuse case.

Assumptions & next steps:
- Numbers assume average 220 tokens/request; if your real average is lower we'll reprice downward.
- We'll instrument a small telemetry snippet (2 endpoints) to capture token distribution and request sizes; Ben will define the exact metrics.
- If procurement approves, sign a short SOW for the pilot and we kick off within a week. I put a HubSpot deal link here for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/642

Attached (and in the shared Drive): redwood_cost_model_v2.xlsx, pilot_ops_checklist.pdf. Ben — can you coordinate the infra deep-dive and share the telemetry snippet?

Thanks — Karthik
